Buffers are measured from the ordinary high water mark and assume a vegetated native plant community. Lakes and ponds over 20 acres are regulated under the SMP.

review.process: No separate critical areas permit when the review is done with a county land use or development permit. Activities that need no other permit are processed as a Type I permit under Ch. 17.05 LCC. Appeals follow the underlying permit.
review.triggers: Review applies when development is within, abutting, or likely to affect a critical area or buffer. Wetland assessment report required within mapped hydric soils or 300 feet of a mapped wetland; aquatic habitat assessment within 200 feet of aquatic habitat; mitigation plan when impacts are proposed. Reports are prepared by a qualified professional and valid for 5 years.
review.exemptions: Activities allowed without a permit or report if they cause no loss of critical area functions: maintenance within existing rights-of-way, minor utility work, forest practices, agriculture covered by the Voluntary Stewardship Program, conservation and restoration, research, invasive plant removal, and emergencies. Small isolated Category IV wetlands (under 4,000 sq ft) are exempt from the avoidance requirement.
review.relief: Buffer reduction or averaging (not both). Impacts beyond the allowed reductions only through a reasonable use exception or variance.

review.process: No permit or approval (building, right-of-way, site development, shoreline permits and others) is granted except in compliance with the chapter. Review occurs with the underlying permit and SEPA/JARPA review; other agency permits are the applicant's responsibility.
review.triggers: Wetland report by a qualified professional when the site includes, is likely to include, or is adjacent to a wetland or wetland buffer. Critical area report when an activity is proposed within a fish and wildlife habitat conservation area or its buffer.
review.exemptions: Exempt activities require a written request approved by the administrator (emergencies, utility maintenance under a memorandum of agreement, and others). Allowed uses such as low-impact recreation are subject to development and mitigation standards. Small isolated Category IV wetlands are exempt from avoidance.

review.process: A site plan review application is required for permit-related procedures and allowed activities. The administrator decides whether critical areas may be affected and whether a critical area report is needed.
review.triggers: Applies to uses and activities within, adjacent to, or likely to affect a critical area, and to activities within a required buffer. rows: Wetlands with a high conservation value

notes: ¹ Interdunal wetlands over 1 acre scoring 8–9 habitat points are rated Category I.

review.process: The administrator first screens for exemptions. Non-exempt activities complete a critical areas and resource lands checklist, followed by a staff site visit. The determination becomes final with the associated permit unless appealed.
review.triggers: Applies to all land uses and development, with or without a permit. A critical area report is required when the checklist, maps, or site visit show critical areas, with additional requirements for wetlands and fish and wildlife habitat conservation areas.
review.exemptions: Exemptions (emergencies and others) and permitted activities in wetlands and FWHCAs. The exemptions do not apply within shoreline jurisdiction.
review.relief: Variance and reasonable use exception (neither available within shoreline jurisdiction); appeals.

tables.title: Stream Buffers
rows: Per SMP Table 2 (minimum shoreline buffer by designation)
Greater than 2 feet and up to 20 feet wide
notes: Buffers are measured above the ordinary high water mark. Averaging may reduce width by no more than 25 percent (RMC 15.18.320).

review.process: No separate critical areas permit. Compliance is a condition of any project permit under Ch. 15.08 RMC; the administrator reviews each project permit application or SEPA threshold decision.
review.triggers: Site visit when a parcel is in or within 300 feet of a critical area. Technical reports by a qualified professional when information is insufficient; a wetland technical report may be required for development adjacent to a wetland, and a habitat management plan for activity in or adjacent to a habitat conservation area.
review.exemptions: Exempt where the critical area is not degraded: conservation and restoration, passive recreation, research, maintenance of existing rights-of-way, roads, utilities and structures, utilities within existing rights-of-way, hazard tree removal, existing agriculture using BMPs, site investigation, and Class 1–3 forest practices.
review.relief: Reasonable use exception (administrator); variances heard by the planning commission under Ch. 15.52 RMC; wetland buffer averaging to no less than 75 percent of the standard width.
